info.title: NewsCatcher Agent API
info.description: Agent runs (events from a query, or news about companies), company lists and monitors. Authenticate with your API key in the x-api-key header.

get.description: Liveness probe.
Report the deployed service version.

post.description:
Start a run. Without `companies`: events from the question (Fast, Standard or Max). With `companies`:
each company's news (`kind: companies`). It runs in the background; follow it with `GET /runs/{run_id}/progress`.

get.description: The caller's runs (events and companies; scheduled monitor runs are under /monitors), newest first.

parameters.name: kind

schema.description: Only runs of this kind (default: both).
schema.title: Kind

parameters.description: Only runs of this kind (default: both).

get.description: One of the caller's runs, with its rows when finished.

patch.description: Rename one of the caller's runs in their history.

delete.description: Delete one of the caller's finished runs: it leaves their history and its content is erased.

get.description:
Live progress as Server-Sent Events: run_status, run_event, run_result, run_error.

Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`) to resume without missing events.

parameters.name: after

schema.description: Resume after this event id (same as Last-Event-ID).
schema.title: After

parameters.description: Resume after this event id (same as Last-Event-ID).

post.description: Cancel a run. A queued run stops at once; a running one before its next step.

get.description: The run's table as CSV: the dataset's rows, or a companies run's stories (one per row, company first).

A companies run's coverage as CSV: one row per company asked for (found, no_news, incomplete,
identity_unknown; pending while it runs, not_searched if it ended before reaching the company).
The run's table as an Excel file: the dataset's rows, or a companies run's stories.
A companies run's coverage as an Excel file: one row per company.
A batch as one run: status, progress, every finished part's stories and companies, and its parts.

delete.description: Delete every part of a finished batch.

get.description: Every part's live progress in one stream (each event's data has `run_id`), then `batch_status`.

parameters.name: after

schema.description: Resume after this event id (same as Last-Event-ID).
schema.title: After

parameters.description: Resume after this event id (same as Last-Event-ID).

get.description: Every finished part's stories as one CSV.

Every company of the batch (coverage; pending until its part ends, not_searched if the part ended before
reaching it) as one CSV.
Every finished part's stories as one Excel file.
Every company of the batch (coverage, or pending until its part ends) as one Excel file.

post.description: Cancel every part that has not ended.

get.description: The caller's lists in the organization they act for, most recently changed first (without companies).

schema.title: Response List Lists Companies Lists Get

post.description: Create a list from companies sent as JSON; new companies are resolved in the background.
Create a list from a file; new companies are resolved in the background.
Save a company run's companies as a list ("Save as list" on a finished or running run).

get.description: A list with a status per company (poll it while `status` is `resolving`).

delete.description: Delete a list (runs and monitors started from it keep their companies).

post.description: Add companies sent as JSON; the new ones are resolved in the background.
Add companies from a file; the new ones are resolved in the background.

patch.description:
Correct a company that resolved to the wrong business, or was not found: its domain, name or other names.
It goes back to pending and is resolved again as this list's own company; runs and monitors from the list use
the correction.

delete.description: Remove a company from a list.

get.description: The caller's monitors in the current organization.

post.description: Create a monitor; it first runs at its next scheduled time (`POST /{id}/run` runs it now).

get.description: One of the caller's monitor runs, with the stories it delivered.
What a monitor run delivered, as CSV (`change` first, then the stories' or rows' columns).
What a monitor run delivered, as an Excel file.
One of the caller's monitors.

patch.description: Change a monitor: name, companies, schedule, settings, or pause and resume it.

delete.description: Delete a monitor (its past runs stay in the caller's history).

post.description: Run a monitor at the scheduler's next tick (within 5 minutes); its schedule then continues as before.

get.description: The monitor's story feed: its companies' stories, most recent first, as its settings filter them.
A dataset monitor's rows: what it delivered and the source run's rows, newest first.
The monitor's past runs, newest first (open one with `GET /monitors/runs/{run_id}`).

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Companies by domain; ones already listed are kept.

BatchDetail.title: BatchDetail
BatchDetail.description:
A batch (a company list too big for one run, split into runs of up to 50 companies) as one run: its status,
progress, every finished part's stories and companies, and its parts.

name.title: Name
name.description: The list's name (default: the file's name).

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: Your own id for the list (a UUID); left out, one is generated.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: A company list's id (a UUID; POST /companies/lists). Companies not resolved yet are waited for; a list bigger than one run allows starts several runs (one batch).

items.title: Items
items.description: Companies by domain, instead of list_id.

save_as_list.title: Save As List
save_as_list.description: Also save the typed items as a company list (returned as list_id).

list_name.title: List Name
list_name.description: The saved list's name (default: the run's name).

CompaniesIn.title: CompaniesIn
CompaniesIn.description: The companies a run finds news about: a company list, or companies typed in.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The company's website, e.g. stripe.com (a URL works too).

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional name; a mismatch with the pinned profile rebuilds it.

CompanyListItemView.title: CompanyListItemView
CompanyListItemView.description: A company in a list, with what the user sees.

CompanyStatus.title: CompanyStatus
CompanyStatus.description: What the user sees per company.

other_names.title: Other Names
other_names.description: Names it also goes by: brands, former or local names (at most 10; [] clears them).

CorrectCompanyRequest.title: CorrectCompanyRequest
CorrectCompanyRequest.description:
PATCH a company in a list that resolved wrong (or was not found): the fields given change, and it is
resolved again as this list's own company (other users' profiles of the domain are not touched).

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: Your own id for the list: a UUID (e.g. crypto.randomUUID()); left out, one is generated. Sending the same id again returns the same list.

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Companies by domain; repeats are dropped.

CreateCompanyListRequest.title: CreateCompanyListRequest
CreateCompanyListRequest.description: Create a list from companies sent as JSON (a file goes to `/companies/lists/upload`).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: companies: their new stories. dataset: re-run a finished research run and deliver its new rows.

name.title: Name
name.description: A name (default: its companies, or its topic).

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Company monitors: at least one (or list_id).

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: Company monitors: a company list's id (a UUID) instead of companies. The monitor follows the list: companies added to or removed from it are monitored from the next run on.

from_run_id.title: From Run Id
from_run_id.description: "Monitor this": one of your succeeded runs. An events run is re-run (same mode and columns); a companies run gives a company monitor of its companies.

query.title: Query
query.description: What to watch for. Company monitors: only stories about this, e.g. "funding and acquisitions" (blank: every story about the companies; from a companies run: its query). Dataset monitors: the research request (blank: the run's query with its time window removed).

topic.title: Topic
topic.description: Deprecated: the old name of query for dataset monitors.

schedule.description: Default: daily at 09:00 UTC; Standard/Max dataset monitors default to weekly (today's weekday), and may run daily too.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Your chat conversation where each run's result is also posted.

CreateMonitorRequest.title: CreateMonitorRequest
CreateMonitorRequest.description: POST /monitors: a company monitor (`companies`) or a dataset monitor (`kind: dataset`, `from_run_id`).

query.title: Query
query.description: What to find, e.g. 'Bank M&A deals announced in the US since Sep 15'. Required without companies. With companies it is optional: only stories about it are kept, e.g. 'funding and acquisitions' (blank: every story about the companies).

companies.description: Find news about these companies instead of events from the question.

lookback_days.title: Lookback Days
lookback_days.description: With companies: how many days back from today (1-365, default 30). Event runs read their time window from the query.

include_market_activity.title: Include Market Activity
include_market_activity.description: With companies: keep market_activity stories (stock moves, analyst ratings; default true).

read_web.title: Read Web
read_web.description: With companies: also read their own newsroom and the web (default true).

recheck_borderline.title: Recheck Borderline
recheck_borderline.description: With companies: a stronger model rechecks borderline web pages for little-covered companies (default true).

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: fast: one agent, about 1-3 minutes. standard: deep research (planned slices, every web page read, each row verified, a cited briefing), about 10-30 minutes. max: deep research with stronger models, higher recall and cost. With companies: standard only (the default there). "default", Standard's name before 0.10.0, is still accepted.

max_rows.title: Max Rows
max_rows.description: Without companies: rows to return at most, in every mode: 50 (default), 100, 150 or 200, up to your plan's cap (100 today; more is refused with too_many_rows). A run is charged per 50 rows delivered past the first 50.

keep_updated.description: Keep it updated: once the run succeeds, the agent makes a monitor of it (a companies run -> a company monitor, following its company list if any; an events run -> a dataset monitor). The run is the monitor's first run; the monitor then delivers only what is new. Its state is the run's keep_updated.

CreateRunRequest.title: CreateRunRequest
CreateRunRequest.description:
POST /runs: one entry point. Without `companies` it finds events from the query (Fast, Standard or
Max); with `companies` it finds each company's news stories (Standard; the query, if any, keeps the stories
about it).

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Every error: a stable code and a message to show the user.

schedule.description: When the monitor delivers (default: daily at 09:00 UTC; Standard/Max events runs: weekly on today's weekday).

name.title: Name
name.description: The monitor's name (default: the run's name).

KeepUpdatedIn.title: KeepUpdatedIn
KeepUpdatedIn.description: Keep the run's results updated: once the run succeeds, the agent makes a monitor of it.

KeepUpdatedOut.title: KeepUpdatedOut
KeepUpdatedOut.description: A run started with keep_updated: its monitor, once made.

name.title: Name
name.description: The list's name (default: the run's name).

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: Your own id for the list (a UUID); left out, one is generated.

ListFromRunRequest.title: ListFromRunRequest
ListFromRunRequest.description: Save a company run's companies as a list.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The company's website domain, e.g. stripe.com.

name.title: Name
name.description: Its name, when the domain alone is ambiguous.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.description: Dataset monitors: topic, columns, mode, max_rows, source_run_id, window_to (where the last complete run ended).

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Its companies now (a list monitor: its list's).

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The company list it follows (companies added to or removed from the list are monitored from the next run on).

query.title: Query
query.description: What it watches for: a company monitor's query (null: every story), a dataset monitor's research request.

paused_reason.title: Paused Reason
paused_reason.description: Why the service paused it: "out_of_credits" (its organization's credits no longer cover it; top up, then resume) or "idle" (the organization's free monitor, its results not opened for 14 days; resume it). Null when running or paused by its user.

last_opened_at.title: Last Opened At
last_opened_at.description: When its owner last opened its runs, stories or rows (the free monitor pauses after 14 days without).

source_run_id.title: Source Run Id
source_run_id.description: The run it was made from ("Keep updated", "Monitor this"): its first run.

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: What each company's refresh did: domain, news_status, created, updated, window.

more.title: More
more.description: New stories beyond this run's cap, delivered by the next run.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: What it delivered, one row each, with change (new | update).

found.title: Found
found.description: Dataset monitors: rows the research found (new ones and repeats).

window_from.title: Window From
window_from.description: Dataset monitors: first day this run covered.

window_to.title: Window To
window_to.description: Dataset monitors: last day this run covered.

MonitorRunDetail.title: MonitorRunDetail
MonitorRunDetail.description:
A monitor run with what it delivered, as the runs' table: `columns` and `rows`, each row with `change`
(`new`, or `update` for a company story that grew since it was delivered). `stories` (company monitors) and
`found` are the older fields, kept for compatibility.

MonitorRunSummary.title: MonitorRunSummary
MonitorRunSummary.description: One of a monitor's runs: a scheduled run, or the run it was made from (its first run).

PhaseTiming.title: PhaseTiming
PhaseTiming.description: One phase of a run with its times (see services/progress.py `phase_timeline`).

RenameRequest.title: RenameRequest
RenameRequest.description: PATCH a run or conversation: its new title in the caller's history.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: Each: row (column -> value), run_id (where it came from), created_at.

RowListResponse.title: RowListResponse
RowListResponse.description: A dataset monitor's rows, newest first.

RunDetail.title: RunDetail
RunDetail.description:
A run with its result: the same table for both kinds. An events run has the columns its question needed; a
companies run has one story per row (company first) and, in `companies`, one row per company.

hours.title: Hours
hours.description: every: hours only: hours between runs, counted from `at` each day. Refused with invalid_schedule below your plan's minimum interval (24 hours on Free and PAYG).

ScheduleIn.title: ScheduleIn
ScheduleIn.description:
When the monitor runs: daily (default) or weekly at a local time in a timezone, or every few hours from that
time when your plan allows runs more often than daily.

include_market_activity.title: Include Market Activity
include_market_activity.description: Also market_activity stories: stock moves and analyst ratings (hidden by default).

SkippedLine.title: SkippedLine
SkippedLine.description: A line of the file that gave no company.

StoryListResponse.title: StoryListResponse
StoryListResponse.description: A monitor's story feed, most recent first.

lead.title: Lead
lead.description: The article shown for it: title, url, source, published.

version.title: Version
version.description: Rises when the story grows materially; a monitor delivers it again then.

StoryOut.title: StoryOut
StoryOut.description: A story about one of the monitor's companies.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: false pauses it, true resumes it.

fill_gap.title: Fill Gap
fill_gap.description: With enabled true on a paused monitor: true covers the days it was paused (its next delivery brings what it missed, up to 30 days); false starts from today (only what is new from now).

query.title: Query
query.description: A company monitor's query ("" for every story); a dataset monitor's research request.

UpdateMonitorRequest.title: UpdateMonitorRequest
UpdateMonitorRequest.description: PATCH /monitors/{id}: only the fields given change.
